summary: A paired phone can approve, not only deny, the approval cards an agent's Switchboard MCP pull request writes open: create_pull_request, reply_to_conversation, resolve_conversation, comment_on_line, draft_review and rerun_check. Rationale: a device with the chat scope can already send the agent full-access turns, which run commands on the desktop; approving a post whose text the card shows is a smaller power. Backend: RESPOND_TO_REQUEST lets a chat-scoped device approve a hostWrite card (was admin), logs which device session approved, and refuses a review approved without a verdict or with one the card did not offer (hostWriteApprovalProblem), leaving the card open so the user can pick again; every later guard (re-checks after the card, plan mode, budget, link rule, expiry, cancel) is unchanged. The Reviews human write channels (PullRequestWriteChannels) stay admin-scoped. The push says 'Needs approval: <write> on <PR>' instead of 'Approve at the desktop', and the plain-text detail no longer ends with 'Answer this on the desktop' (both phone cards say what applies themselves) Wire: the phone reuses the RESPOND_TO_REQUEST 4th argument (parseHostWriteResponse) and sends only resolve (reply) or verdict (review); it never edits. Compatibility: the backend adds the ready capability agent_host_write_phone_approval_v1; a phone offers Approve on a hostWrite card only when the backend advertises it, so a newer phone on an older desktop keeps the Deny-only card, and an older Expo phone on a newer desktop keeps its own Deny-only card. An older native Android app already showed Approve on these cards (the backend refused it); on a newer backend that Approve now posts the agent's draft as shown, except a review, which is refused for want of a verdict. Expo: the card shows the write's title, host / PR / location, the detail, an action-named primary button, 'Post and resolve' for a reply, and for draft_review one button per offered verdict with none primary, a verdict that cannot go as drafted disabled with the reason. Android: the same in its approval row (HostWriteCards.kt ports shared/host-write-phone.ts).

automated: npm run typecheck and npm test -- --maxWorkers=2 (root vitest): agent-approvals (a chat-scope phone approves a host write as drafted; a review needs a verdict and refuses one the card did not offer, keeping the card open; a device without the scope is refused and may still deny), switchboard-mcp-integration (through ProviderRegistry and the real MCP bridge: a remote device with no scopes is refused, a phone with the chat scope approves a reply as drafted and it posts the agent's text with the marker, against a fake Reviews service), mcp-pr-tools (a review approved without a verdict or with an unknown one, and an author's Approve, are refused at the card and nothing posts), device-auth (every PullRequestWriteChannels channel stays admin-only while RESPOND_TO_REQUEST is open to a phone), agent-host-writes (phoneHostWriteButtons labels, primaries, responses and the verdict problem; hostWriteApprovalProblem; the push text), mobile-approval-actions (Approve only with the capability, Deny only for the legacy cached flag, the capability is in BACKEND_CAPABILITIES), mobile-chat-store (the hostWrite card rides on the approval row).

npm test --prefix apps/mobile (jest, feed-items): the ordinary card offers Approve and Deny; a hostWrite card on a backend without the capability, or a legacy desktopOnly row, offers Deny only; a reply card names the write and context, offers Post reply and Post and resolve, says Edit on the desktop, and a tap sends { resolve: true }; a review offers Comment, Request changes and Approve and a tap sends the verdict; an author's review offers Comment only.

./gradlew --offline testDebugUnitTest (apps/android): HostWriteCardsTest (decode, title, context, buttons, review verdicts and problems, response JSON), ThreadInteractionPolicyTest (approvalActions by capability, the response on the UI action), ThreadSessionCoordinatorTest (the response reaches the remote; backendTakesPhoneApproval from the capability), SwitchboardRemoteClientTest (the 4th RESPOND_TO_REQUEST argument), CachedThreadStateMapperTest (a cached hostWrite card is restored). ./gradlew lintDebug compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin passed.
notExercised: No phone or emulator was run: the Expo card was checked through jest renders only and the Android card through unit tests of its policy; the Compose ApprovalRow layout (FlowRow of buttons) was compiled but not looked at.
No real GitHub or Bitbucket write was made; every host call in the tests ran against fakes.

Release lanes (docs/releasing.md): the Expo app is the iOS client and its change is JS only (no native module, permission or app.json change, so the fingerprint is unchanged), so it ships over mobile-ota.yml (EAS update, --platform ios). Native Android needs a signed APK: bump versionName / versionCode and dispatch mobile-release.yml. Neither release was run.
